clue.text: Possibly help great paper marking its 10 Down 11 Down today

definitions.text: paper marking its 10 Down 11 Down today

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters before it are only one possible order of the word, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A newspaper congratulates itself on a big anniversary of its puzzle, perhaps a great help to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential clue: this puzzle was the Telegraph's celebration of its crossword's hundredth birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is the British newspaper whose crossword reached its centenary on the day this puzzle ran.

clue.text: Puzzle cracked in game

indicators.note: something cracked is broken open, so the letters that follow are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: A puzzle solved during play, like a code broken mid-game.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, so the word is a synonym for a puzzle.

clue.text: Name taken by setter in a novel delights

indicators.note: one thing taken by another goes along with it, so these pieces are joined side by side
'novel' means new, so the gathered letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter who appears by name in a novel is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to amuse or please them, so entertains is a synonym of the verb delights.

clue.text: Make a mistake holding answer back? That's unusual

indicators.note: something holding another wraps around it, so one piece sits inside the other
'back' tells the solver to read the combined letters from the end to the start

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone holding back an answer for fear of being wrong does something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes inside ERR to make ERAR, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is seldom found or seen, which is what unusual means.

clue.text: Tap up niece playing game

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom to the top, so backwards
letters that are playing are moving about freely, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
taken as written as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An uncle gives his niece a pat while she plays a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap up' reads like a phrasal verb meaning to approach someone, but it is a word plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the British name for solitaire, a card game played by one person.

clue.text: Editor is working for creator who made light of his work?

definitions.text: creator who made light of his work?

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
taken as written
a machine that is working is switched on

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is busy on behalf of someone who joked about their own job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made light of' usually means treated as trivial; here it literally means produced light, as with the light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor famous for developing a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: Root used to be a bit short

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter of the preceding word is dropped

blocks.note: 'was' is the past tense of be
taken as written
taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A plant root that once was a little too small.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a Japanese plant whose pungent green root is grated as a condiment, so the answer is a root.

clue.text: 1 Across 10 Down solver maybe read dictionary (but not all of it)

indicators.note: taking only part of the words means the needed letters sit inside them, run across the gap

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A puzzle fan might browse a dictionary without reading the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on doing the Telegraph puzzle every day is, playfully, an addict of it, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Tackling the 1 Across 10 Down could be one element of spirituality

indicators.note: an element is a part of a whole, so the letters wanted are a run lying inside the next word

blocks.note: a run of six letters from inside the word

explanation.surface: Doing the daily puzzle might count as part of one's spiritual life.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a habitual act repeated in the same way, as a daily crossword is for many solvers; an example of the definition.

clue.text: Challenge laid out in black and white?

definitions.text: Challenge laid out in black and white?

blocks.clueFragment: Challenge laid out in black and white?
blocks.note: surface reading: a challenge written down clearly, set out in plain print

blocks.clueFragment: laid out in black and white
blocks.note: setter's reading: a puzzle laid out on a grid of black and white squares

explanation.walkthrough: 'In black and white' usually means in writing; here it describes the grid of the puzzle itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic puzzle is a challenge printed on a grid of dark and light squares, so this describes the thing itself.

clue.text: Any centre free for today's milestone

indicators.note: letters set free are loose to move, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: Any venue offered free of charge for a celebration today.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary is a hundredth anniversary, the milestone the Telegraph crossword reached on this day.

clue.text: Mount attack again

blocks.note: to rush is to charge at
once more, again

explanation.surface: An order to climb up and charge a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as a verb, as in mount an attack, but it is the title of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota is the mountain carved with four presidents' faces, so the answer names a mount.

clue.text: Resolve to get answer for one in twenties?

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in where the other was

blocks.note: to resolve to do something is to decide
A is the usual abbreviation for answer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in their twenties determined to find the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in DECIDE is replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are a span of ten years, so a period such as the 1920s is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Reserve writer beginning to rattle you, say

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a sub, or substitute, is a reserve player
a scribe is one who writes
opening letter

explanation.surface: A backup author starts to unsettle the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A Telegraph reader who pays regularly for the paper is a subscriber, so 'you' is an example of the answer.

clue.text: In France, the fourth Down clue reportedly bored

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as heard said, so the word is one that is pronounced like the clue's idea

blocks.clueFragment: In France, the fourth Down clue
blocks.note: the fourth down clue is 5 Down, and five in French is cinq

explanation.surface: A French solver is bored by the fourth down clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the down clues in order: 2, 3, 4, 5 — the fourth is numbered 5, and the French for five sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a well or shaft is to bore it, so the past tense of sink matches bored.

clue.text: Staff pictures laid out without English text

indicators.note: things laid out are spread and arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order
'without' means lacking, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: to man a post is to staff it
taken as written as the material
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Office workers' photos are arranged with no English caption.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from PICTURES, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is a written or typed text, especially an author's original before printing.

clue.text: Row after boss's big and bold words?

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second, so the order of joining is reversed from the clue

blocks.note: the head is the boss; the 's links to the next word
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: A quarrel follows the boss's loud, aggressive language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel and 'big and bold words' like boasting, but the row is a line and the words are in large print.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title printed in large heavy type above a newspaper story.

clue.text: Fierce eagles traversing small desert

indicators.note: something traversing moves across to the far side, so the next piece lines up straight after

blocks.note: wild animals are fierce
an erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Ferocious eagles flying over a small patch of desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild, uninhabited land, and a desert in the old sense is just such a deserted place.

clue.text: Not as busy in class

blocks.note: 'not as much' is less
someone who is on is engaged or occupied

explanation.surface: A pupil less occupied than usual during class.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, which is what a class is in a school timetable.

clue.text: Clear over what's used to fill in a 1 Across 10 Down?

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

blocks.clueFragment: what's used to fill in a 1 Across 10 Down?
blocks.note: the tool many solvers write their answers with

explanation.surface: A solver wonders what to use to finish the grid once it is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, and scorecards shorten it to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Open ground is clear of obstacles, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Square meal featured in article? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: a thing featured in another appears inside it; 'quite the opposite' then flips which piece goes inside which

blocks.note: an Italian dish eaten as a meal
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a hearty, traditional meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' reverses the instruction: the article goes inside the meal, not the meal inside the article.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is a public square or open marketplace, especially in an Italian town.

clue.text: Stress of a compiler initially with little money

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: The worry of a poorly paid crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is emphasis laid on a syllable, which is the sense of stress in speech.

clue.text: Live on part of a square, perhaps

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a square has four sides; 'perhaps' since many shapes do

explanation.surface: Living in one corner of a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have one's home there, so it is a synonym of the verb live.

clue.text: Shock after a jolly century – comfortable place to solve?

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second, so the first-named piece goes on the end

blocks.note: taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: Surprise at a festive hundredth anniversary, celebrated from a cosy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the century, but it is slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a padded seat with arm rests, a cosy spot where many solvers sit with the paper.

clue.text: Destiny, by the sound of it, for 28 Across

indicators.note: a word known by its sound is one heard rather than spelt, so a same-sounding word is wanted

blocks.note: one's fate is one's destiny

explanation.surface: A prediction of what lies ahead for a cross-referenced answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or celebrate them publicly, so the verb is a synonym of the answer at 28 Across.

clue.text: Cell somewhere in Alabama

blocks.note: first meaning: a cell phone, a portable telephone
second meaning: a port city on the Gulf coast of that state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison cell in Alabama, but it is short for a cellphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellphone is called a mobile in Britain, and Mobile is a city on Alabama's coast.

clue.text: Cheeses said to give you what the 1 Across 10 Down shouldn't be?

definitions.text: what the 1 Across 10 Down shouldn't be?

indicators.note: 'said' means spoken, so the word wanted is one heard the same as the fodder

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Cheese talk somehow tells us how hard the daily puzzle ought to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is something very easy, and a good daily cryptic should offer some resistance rather than be a pushover.

clue.text: Observe the price of fame?

indicators.note: 'of' here simply links the two pieces, read in the order the phrase is turned round

blocks.note: a celeb, a celebrity, is someone with fame
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: Pondering the cost of being famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the price of fame' as a famous person's fee, and the pieces fall into place.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to celebrate it, as one marks this centenary.
